title: Which lines start a job
prompt: What does this program print? `jobs()` counts the jobs started so far in the program's job group. Two of the 12 lesson trips were paid in cash, by two different drivers. Type each printed line on its own line.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false")
sc = spark.sparkContext
tracker = sc.statusTracker()
sc.setJobGroup("lines", "which lines start a job")


def jobs():
    return len(tracker.getJobIdsForGroup("lines"))


cash = trips.filter(F.col("payment_type") == "cash").select("trip_id", "driver_id")
by_driver = cash.groupBy("driver_id").count()
top = by_driver.limit(1)
print(jobs())

plan = top._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
print(jobs())

n = cash.count()
print(jobs())

first = cash.first()
rows = by_driver.collect()
print(jobs())
print(n, first["trip_id"], len(rows))
hints: `filter`, `select`, `groupBy(...).count()` and `limit` all give back a new DataFrame. None of them runs anything.
Building a plan as text only plans the work; it doesn't run it.
`count()` on a DataFrame, `first()` and `collect()` each start one job here.
explanation: The first three lines only describe work: `filter`, `select`, `groupBy(...).count()` and `limit` each return a new DataFrame, so the count is still 0. Turning the physical plan into text plans the query but runs no job, so it's still 0. `cash.count()` is an action, so 1. `first()` and `collect()` are one job each, so 3. The cash trips are T003 and T008, and they have two different drivers, so `by_driver` has 2 rows.
